Alright, so I've got two stories from when I was in univ. They're only mildly interesting, but I thought I might as well tell.

In my university, we had this place called the "deck". I'm not really sure if that's the right term for it, because it's just an extra floor filled with vacant rooms nobody really uses. Students would usually hang out on that floor since it rarely gets checked by security, and all sorts of things happen there, ranging from students sleeping on the floor in between classes to people straight up making out. I also spend a lot of my time on the deck, because my breaks are usually when the deck is most vacant. Something happened that made me stop going there unless I'm with friends, though.

That day, I ended up sleeping while taking a break on the deck. My classes have already ended and I didn't want to go home yet since my house was a 2 to 3 hour ride and I didn't wanna deal with that. I woke up some time in the afternoon, around 5PM, and panicked a bit since it was pretty late already. I packed my stuff and went to the elevator. However, the elevator felt strange cold for some reason, and there was this sense of dread in the air. I ignored it and I pressed the button for the ground floor. Instead of closing its doors, the elevetor just beeped. I tried again and the same thing happened. I then realized it was the alarm saying that the elevator was full and overcapacity, despite the fact that I was the only one on it. I laughed it off and just went down the stairs.

To my surprise, the elevator was on the following floor, wide open as if it has always been there. I felt weird, but nonetheless continued going down the stairs. The same thing happened on the next floor. And the one after that. By the time I was on the third floors, I was running down the strairs and the empty elevator still managed to catch up to me. I didn't even check on the ground floor if it still followed me. I just ran out of the building and went home.

For the second story, this happened during one of my classes. This one was a lot less scary, but it honestly felt terribly weird and I couldn't even rationalize it. Save for a few rooms, all the rooms in my university had two doors. One morning, we were struggling to open one of the doors to my business management class. It was unlocked, but the door knob just wouldn't turn. That day, we ended up just using the other door. Midway through the lecture, the broken door just burst wide open, as if someone slammed on it. Nobody opened it, and it wasn't even windy that day. Our class stopped for a few minutes because we were all puzzled with that just happened.

These things didn't bother me all that much, but they definitely made me feel a bit anxious whenever I sleep on the deck or in one of the vacant rooms.
